sources.title: DuckDB documentation: Reading Faulty CSV Files (docs/current)
sources.pin: sha256:12897abe4612269153224a487dd74a46c1143b3be1824132a7ee00e1838778ad (branch main @ 2026-10-06; 'current' docs = DuckDB 1.5 per rendered-site version selector in companion capture)
locators: 'By default, when performing a CSV read, if any structural errors are encountered, the scanner will immediately stop the scanning process and throw the error'
'Using the ignore_errors Option': 'rows containing data that would otherwise cause the CSV parser to generate an error will be ignored'
Projection pushdown caveat: selecting only 'name' makes both rows valid because 'the casting error on the age would never occur'
'Retrieving Faulty CSV Lines': store_rejects; reject_errors columns: line, line_byte_position, byte_position, column_idx, column_name, error_type, csv_line, error_message
Error example output shows sample_size=20480 and suggests sample_size=-1 for full-scan auto-detection; LINE SIZE OVER MAXIMUM default 2,097,152 bytes

sources.title: PR #10777 diff — CSV sniffer fix for ignore_errors=true (issue #10769)
sources.pin: capture sha256:6c7c1314e258223be7de65378b6e1429b20567a0d13a791d64be9c698dc1d771 (full diff, 63,948 bytes; both halves read by candidate)
locators: new fixture data/csv/titanic.csv (892 data rows added)

src/execution/operator/csv_scanner/sniffer/type_detection.cpp: adds 'idx_t min_errors = NumericLimits<idx_t>::Maximum();' and guards candidate selection with '(!options.ignore_errors || candidate->error_handler->errors.size() < min_errors)' so the sniffer prefers dialects generating the fewest errors when ignore_errors=true
test/sql/copy/csv/test_ignore_errors.test: extends with 'query IIIIIIIIIIII' / "FROM read_csv('data/csv/titanic.csv', ignore_errors=1) limit 10" and 10 expected rows (regression test)
sources.used_for: Fix + regression-test evidence in the issue chain
sources.limits: Diff proves what changed in the PR; it does not by itself prove which release contains it — release membership established separately by S6

sources.title: PEP 751 – A file format to record Python dependencies for installation reproducibility (Status: Final)
sources.pin: capture sha256:a73937a1e942c22f3a4c623dd59d3a7008b7f85f1bbf293c50a966e7a1257ce0 (first 32,768 of 162,130 bytes; cited sections in delivered text); etag "6ac147a7-27952", Last-Modified Sat, 03 Oct 2026
locators: Header: Status 'Final', Standards Track, Created 24-Jul-2024, Resolution 31-Mar-2025

Abstract: format 'designed to be human-readable and machine-generated. Installers consuming the file should be able to calculate what to install without the need for dependency resolution at install-time.'
Specification > File Name: MUST be named pylock.toml or match ^pylock\.([^.]+)\.toml$
Motivation: requirements files 'not a standard but ... supported by convention ... not secure by default (file hash support is entirely an opt-in feature)'
Banner: canonical, up-to-date spec maintained at PyPA specs page (packaging.python.org pylock.toml Specification)
sources.used_for: Environment binding (§3, §9): pylock.toml as pinned, hash-carrying, machine-generated env interchange
sources.limits: Partial capture (spec details beyond File Name/sections not all read); PEP page notes canonical spec moved to PyPA — implementation/tool support status not established here (see leads L7)
